What's amazing about Giganotosaurus?

Possibly even larger than Tyrannosaurus, Giganotosaurus was an enormous dinosaur that lived in South America. Its blade-like teeth are its defining feature.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Giganotosaurus

Giganotosaurus lived in South America (Argentina) about 98 million years ago. Around 12–14 m long and weighing 6–8 tons, it may have been bigger than T. rex. Its teeth were blade-shaped for slicing flesh, and its front arms had three fingers with sharp claws. It may even have hunted in packs, taking down the giant plant-eating Argentinosaurus. Its fossil was discovered by an amateur collector in 1994.

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Find Argentina on a map and compare its size with T. rex. Comparing each dinosaur's different weapon — "blade-like teeth vs. thick teeth" — makes it even more fascinating.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How big was Giganotosaurus?
A. About 12–14 m long — it may have been bigger than Tyrannosaurus. It lived in South America.

Q. Were its teeth different from Tyrannosaurus's?
A. Yes. They were blade-shaped for slicing flesh. Its hunting style differed from T. rex's thick teeth.

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Find Argentina on a map, and compare its size and teeth with T. rex.
